tools.name: workflow_state
tools.description: Whether the bridge is working: where it lives, app version, snapshot age. check: "ping" round-trips one command to the app; "doctor" checks this computer end to end (sign-in, publishing, version, scheduled jobs, Claude Code, monitors) and says how to fix anything wrong. Use this first if anything else fails.

tools.name: workflow_queue
tools.description: Your inbox as "Companion", led by the user's house rules (standing instructions for every assistant; follow them within your normal judgement): tasks assigned to Companion, tasks whose recent comments say @Companion, notes that say @Companion, and watches that came due — each with why it's here, its status line, checklist and latest comment. Work meant for another agent is not yours.

tools.name: workflow_list
tools.description: List or search. kind: tasks (default; open ones unless all), notes (the Notepad; '*' marks ones addressed to you), projects (status, dates, progress, health and why), documents (every file; query also matches WF-numbers, profiles and the text inside PDFs and scans), comments (what people wrote since a time, default the last 24 h, not your own). query, project and status narrow tasks, notes and documents.

tools.name: workflow_get
tools.description: One task (with checklist and comment thread), note, or document (profile, folder, versions, start of its text) in full. Give an id, a WF-number, or a fragment of its title; kind settles a fragment that could be more than one.

tools.name: workflow_create_task
tools.description: Create a task. Set assignee to "Companion" to put it in your own queue.

comment.description: An opening comment on the new task

tools.name: workflow_update_task
tools.description: Change a task. Only what you pass is touched. status_line overwrites the one-line 'where this stands' pinned above its comments: update it as work progresses rather than commenting each time. Checklist: check_subtasks / uncheck_subtasks / remove_subtasks take exact titles or fragments only one row contains (anything ambiguous is left alone); rename_subtasks fixes a row's wording and keeps its tick. 'notes' REPLACES the notes; prefer append_notes, which keeps the user's formatting. status "Completed" completes it.

notes.description: replaces the notes; empty string clears them

project.description: empty string removes it from its project

tools.name: workflow_comment
tools.description: Post a comment on a task, as you. This is how you reply to the user: it reaches their phone. hand_to gives the task to another assistant (Claude, or a companion such as Jarvis) or a person instead: they become the assignee and your text goes with it; handing to an assistant starts its session. Use hand_to, not an @mention, when the work itself should move.

tools.name: workflow_note
tools.description: The Notepad. action create files a note: where output that isn't work belongs (a summary, a finding, options); use a task for anything that needs doing. reply answers a note inside it (a signed, dated reply appended; notes have no thread, so this is how a note gets an answer). convert promotes a note into a linked task, which is what takes it out of the inbox. Read notes with workflow_list / workflow_get.

tools.name: workflow_create_project
tools.description: Create a project, or update an existing one of the same name.

start.description: planned start yyyy-MM-dd, or 'none' to clear

target.description: target date yyyy-MM-dd, or 'none' to clear

tools.name: workflow_attach
tools.description: Put a file from this computer into WorkFlow. Give one of: task (attaches it), project (files it in the project's workspace, with an optional profile and folder), or document (uploads a new version; the old one stays in its history, profile and folder carry over).

file.description: Path to the file on this computer

name.description: display name; defaults to the filename

tools.name: workflow_update_document
tools.description: Change a document's profile or folder. Profile fields apply to every version; 'name' renames the current file. Folders nest with '/', and '' unfiles.

type.description: Contract, Agreement, Invoice, Quote, Receipt, Letter, Email, Report, Proposal, Minutes, Specification, Drawing, Photo, Form, Policy, Other — or your own

status.description: Draft, In Review, Final, Signed, Superseded

tools.name: workflow_draft_email
tools.description: Prepare an email a task asks for. It is attached to the task as a draft the user checks and sends with Review & Send; nothing is sent from here. Refused unless the user has set Settings → Agent Bridge → Email to Draft Only or Can Send.

tools.name: workflow_watch
tools.description: Set a task aside and be woken to look at it again later: "tell me when the release merges, check every hour", "remind me at 15:00". Give minutes from now or a time (ISO-8601, or HH:MM today). At that time a session starts on this task with "your watch came due"; check the condition, tell the user if it's met, and call this again to re-arm, since a watch fires once. clear: true ends one. Write in the task's status line what you're watching for, so a later session knows. Needs WorkFlow 5.4.

note.description: What you're watching for, shown on the task

tools.name: workflow_monitor
tools.description: Checks that run on this computer every few minutes without using Claude, and wake you only when something changes: a website (http), a port (host:port), free disk space (disk, min_free_gb), a running process, or a file changing. Changes are posted on the task you name. action: add | list | remove. Command monitors can only be added by the person at this computer.

target.description: URL, host:port, folder, process name or file

wake.description: start a session when it changes

expect_text.description: http: text the page must contain

tools.name: workflow_approval
tools.description: Ask the user to approve one command before it runs on this computer (restart a service, install an update, delete old backups). action request posts the exact command on the task with a code, then stop: you're woken when the user replies "approve CODE" or "decline CODE", and only their reply counts. check says where a code stands. run runs an approved command exactly as approved, once, and returns its exit code and output for you to report in the thread. Off unless the user has switched approvals on here.

purpose.description: request: what it does, in plain words
